I.}}</noinclude>the lambe of God. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=37}}† And the tvvo Disciples heard him speaking, and they folovved {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=38}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} turning, and seeing them folowing him, saith to them, VVhat seeke you? VVho said to him, Rabbi (vvhich is called by interpretation, Maister) vvhere dvvellest thou? {{verse|chapter=1|verse=39}}† He saith to them, Come and see. They came, and savv where he abode and they taried vvith him that day: and it vvas about the tenth houre. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=40}}† And Andrevv the brother of Simon Peter vvas one of the tvvo that had heard of Iohn, and folovved him. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=41}}† He findeth first his brother Simon, and saith to him, VVe haue found {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Messias in Hebrue, in Greeke Christ, in English Anointed, to witte, with the spiritual oile of grace aboue his brethren. ''Ps. 44''.}}∷ {{sc|Messias}}, vvhich is being interpreted, {{sc|Christ}}. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=42}}† And he brought him to {{sc|Iesvs}}. And {{sc|Iesvs}} {{sup|‖}} looking vpon him, said, Thou art Simon the sonne of Iona: thou shalt be called {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Cephas in Syriake, & Peter in Greeke, in English Rocke. See Mat. 16, 18.}}∷ ''Cephas'', vvhich is interpreted, Peter. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=43}}† On the morovv he vvould goe forth into Galilee, and he findeth Philippe. And {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to him, Folovv me. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=44}}† And Philippe vvas of Bethsaida, the citie of Andrevv and Peter. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=45}}† Philippe findeth Nathanael, and saith to him, Him vvhom Moyses in the lavv, and the Prophets vvrote of: vve haue found {{sc|Iesvs}} the sonne of Ioseph, of Nazareth. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=46}}† And Nathanael said to him, From Nazareth can there be any good? Philippe saith to him, Come and see. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=47}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Gospel in a votiue Masse of the holy Angels.}}∷ {{sc|Iesvs}} savv Nathanael comming to him, and he saith of him, Behold an Israelite in very deede, in vvhom there is no guile. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=48}}† Nathanael saith to him, Hovv knovvest thou me? {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvered and said to him, Before that Philippe did cal thee, vvhen thou wast vnder the figtree, I saw thee. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=49}}† Nathanael ansvvered him, and saith, Rabbi, thou art the sonne of God, thou art the king of Israel. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=50}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvered, and said to him, Because I said vnto thee, I savv thee vnder the figtree, thou beleeuest: greater then these things shalt thou see. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=51}}† And he saith to him, Amen Amen I say to you, You shal see the heauen opened, and the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 28, 12.''}}* Angels of God ascending and descending, vpon the Sonne of man.⊣

''1. Was the word.''] The second Person in Trinitie which is the natural, onely, and eternal Sonne of God the Father, is called the {{sc|Word}}: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=How God the Sonne is called the WORD.}}not as the holy Scriptures or speaches of the Prophets and Apostles (vvritten and spoken by Gods commaundement for the vttering of his diuine wil towards man) be called his word, but in a more diuine, eminent, and ineffable sort, to expresse vnto<noinclude>{{rh|||vs}}</noinclude>
